title: Check-in for a 10 minute step: no "10 minutes starts in about 10 minutes"

history.text: Riley! 10 minutes of business articles at your desk at 12:30 tomorrow. Locked in.

plan.reason: Ten minutes at lunch keeps you sharp without eating your break.

whatWentWrong: "Your 10 minutes of business articles starts in about 10 minutes." (the step's length and the lead time are both "10 minutes", and "starts" doesn't agree with "minutes")
shouldHaveHappened: The morning kickoff and the check-in before 12:30 each read naturally. The check-in says the articles are coming up soon (around 12:30) without stacking the same phrase twice, such as "10 minutes" for both the step's length and how soon it starts, and with no grammar slips. The timing is right: it doesn't say the step is now or that it already started.
